segments.text: An observational study followed 62 technicians for 12 weeks using self-reported repair logs. Completed repair tasks could include help from colleagues. Checklist use was not recorded, and independent assembly competence was not tested.

Fewer reported procedural hesitations were associated with more completed repair tasks after adjustment for prior experience. The supplied excerpt contains no numerical estimate or confidence interval.
The observation concerns completed repair tasks over twelve weeks, not error frequency during first-session assembly. It does not identify the effect of a guidance checklist.
